How to run a ludus that lasts. The notes at the end come from a 16-season test run of the league.
12 weeks. Each week is a Match Week, Flavius's travelling games: the Undercard on Friday, the Feature on Saturday and the Main event on Sunday. Wins are worth 3 points and runner-up finishes 1.
The top four go to the Superbus. After it come the awards and the recap paper, and then the Quaestor's Ledger pays every house for its season.
A new career opens with its founding ledger, which shows your starting treasury.
Wages are the bill, purses are the income. A fighter rated 60 asks about 14 coin a week, and an Undercard win pays about 30.
Keep your weekly wages below what one good night pays. A small house runs best on about three fighters.
Appearance fees are paid win or lose, so enter someone every week.
Pay blood money only for a fighter you can't replace.
Three week-ends in the red closes the ludus. At the season's close, the creditors count what the Quaestor still owes you.
A house built from nothing opens with 100 coin: the founding treasury plus the Senate's newcomer grant.
Spar every week. The gate from watching fighters is safe income, and the sparring fighter gets an edge on Match Week.
Take the road offers. Another house pays your travel if you enter the fighter they ask for. Struggling houses get these offers more often.
Small houses (2 fighters or fewer, under 120 coin) pay half the blood money to save a condemned fighter.
Your first, partial season is forgiven if it ends in debt. The next one isn't.
In a 20-career test, new houses that spar, take road offers and borrow once survived three seasons 18 times out of 20. Before this build it was 2 out of 20.
Small (2–4 fighters). Enter your best fighter in the bout they fit. Keep weekly wages at or below one night's purse. This is where every house starts.
Medium (5–7). You can fill all three bouts every week and still cover injuries.
Bench the spares and lend them out for a fee.
It pays only with steady Feature and Main event wins. Wages run about 70–100 coin a week.
Large (8+). Build to this once you're thriving.
Special events and exhibitions give the extra fighters bouts, and loans turn the bench into income.
Build Barracks so fighters sign for less, and Practice stands so sparring pays.
There's no cap on signings, but past five fighters, recruits who care about time on the sand grade you a little lower for each extra body.
Thriving houses (350+ coin, or fame 55+ with 150+ coin) are on their own: no loan offers, no cart, no one pays your road, and no Senate stipend.
Starters are the fighters you can enter on Match Week.
Bench fighters train, or go on loan to a friendly house for a weekly fee. Rivals never get a loan.
The injured sit out until they're healed.
The Loans panel shows who is out, who is in, the fee and the weeks left.
A practice bout grows a fighter a little.
League fighters who come to watch each pay a coin from their own purses, 2 with Practice stands.
The fighter who sparred takes +1 AP and +2 CF into this week's Match Week. Spar the fighter you're about to enter.
Lose everyone and a friendly house writes to offer a fighter on loan. You decide whether to accept.
Vulso's cart also comes to your gate once, with three cheap lots and no travel cost.
A loaned fighter goes home as soon as you sign one of your own.
If a loaned fighter dies under your colours, you owe their house a fee.
The physicians have a weekly budget. The Valetudinarium raises it.
Hygeia's Blessing heals your whole roster once a season, for free. Save it for a bad week near the run-in. Every house has one.
Fame opens doors to recruits, but at every season's close it drifts back toward 35. Keep winning to hold it.
Rich houses build: Practice stands pay, the yard trains, the armory adds AP. Once your treasury clears the next building's price, the rival houses are already pouring stone.
Ratings hold steady at a league average of 60–65. A 90+ star appears now and then.
The free-agent market settles at about 55–60 fighters.
House treasuries settle at a median of 150–250.
A house that enters every fighter in every bout and pays every blood price loses about 60 coin a week. Pick your bouts.
Fame crept toward the ceiling for every house. It now drifts back toward 35 each season.
Rich houses sat on 900–1,000 coin. They now build sooner.
The free-agent pool swelled past 75. It's now trimmed to 55.

Beasts are the savings account: gladiators with 2+ beast trophies won 29% and reached the Ludus 45% of the time — with none, 18% and 22%.
Break pots: 2+ pots broken meant 32% wins and 44% Ludus, against 12% and 24% for the pot-shy.
Draw cards: 2+ arena cards won 27% against 18% for coin-only turns.

Ratings: a Luck perk (+1 coin a turn) won 30% against 24% without, and a Charisma perk (+1 CF a turn) 30% with 26 CF on average. A lone +1 movement or +1 damage changes little by itself: spend it early, in the rounds that allow it.
